data.prompt: Run your `merge_sorted` function on the smallest edge cases: `merge_sorted([], [])`, `merge_sorted([1], [])`, and `merge_sorted([], [2])`. Observe whether an exception is raised and, if so, note the exact line and the values of `i`, `j`, `len(a)`, and `len(b)` at that moment.
data.trace_question: What are the maximum values that the expressions `a[i]` and `b[j]` can take during the loop, and do those values ever equal `len(a)` or `len(b)`?
data.expected_insight: The loop condition `while i <= len(a) and j <= len(b)` allows `i` or `j` to become equal to the length of the list, so `a[i]` or `b[j]` can be accessed at index `len(a)` or `len(b)`, which is out of bounds and causes the IndexError.
